name: parameters
about: Parameters for generate(). Every combination yields one connected, closed mesh (occasionally with a few non-manifold edges where thin parts touch; slicers repair these). Unspecified parameters take their defaults.
units: Scene units, Y up, centred on the origin. The longest outer side equals size. toSTL rescales (default longest side 60 mm, Z up).

groups.skeleton: The core lines or points the shape is built on.
groups.flesh: The material wrapped around the skeleton: thickness, cross-section, joints, membranes, holes.
groups.network: Subdividing faces into lattices, growing struts, thinning.
groups.symmetry: How many times the shape repeats around the vertical axis. Noise follows the same symmetry.
groups.noise: Hand-made irregularity: bent skeleton lines and lumpy flesh.
groups.finish: Colour and surface finish. These do not change the geometry.

parameters.description: Skeleton type. Decides what the other parameters act on.

options.description: Points (1–4, see count) with round flesh: a soft lump or cluster of lumps.
Part of a circle; arc sets the opening angle in degrees.
A coil spring. Turns = arc / 110 (330 gives 3 turns). height sets the pitch.
One closed horizontal ring or polygon (sides). Flat: height has no effect.
Two horizontal polygons (sides) joined by vertical posts. Box, cylinder (bulge 1), tray, cage.
A horizontal polygon whose corners meet at one apex above.
Apexes above and below a horizontal polygon (an abacus bead / octahedron with sides 4).
Arms radiating from the centre (sides = number of arms). height ≥ 0.45 adds arms up and down.

parameters.description: Polygon sides, or number of arms for star. 3 = triangle … 8 = octagon.
Number of points for blob (1–4).

Bends the horizontal polygon edges: negative curves them inward (star-like), positive outward, 1 = circle. Only horizontal polygon edges bend; vertical posts and slanted edges stay straight (a bipyramid never becomes a sphere).
arc: opening angle in degrees. helix: number of turns = value / 110.
Overall size. The whole shape is scaled so that its longest outer side equals this value.

Height ratio; small = flat, large = tall. The effect depends on base (outer height ÷ width, approx.): prism/pyramid/bipyramid ≈ value × 0.5 (so 1.6 → 0.8, never a full cube); helix ≈ value × 1.6; star and blob ≈ value (star is flat below 0.45); no effect on loop, line, arc.
Depth ratio: squashes the shape front-to-back (Z) only. 1 = unchanged; smaller = flatter (circle ring → ellipse, square → rectangle). Flesh thickness is kept.
Flesh thickness around the skeleton lines: small = thin wire, large = chunky.
Cross-section of the flesh: 0 = round, 1 = square.
How thickness varies along each line: negative = thick in the middle (spindle), positive = thick at the ends/joints. A line with taper 1 makes a dumbbell.
Rounding where lines meet: 0 = sharp joints, 2 = smoothly melted together.
Fraction of polygon faces covered by a thin plate (0 = wire only, 1 = all faces). Below 1, which faces get a plate is random (depends on seed) unless membraneFaces is set.

Which faces get plates (membrane must be > 0). 0 random (by fraction); 1 sides only (prism → open tube, pyramid → open-bottom canopy); 2 all but upward-facing horizontal faces (prism → open-top box / vessel; low height → tray); 3 horizontal faces only (prism → lidded cage).
Plate thickness, relative to flesh thickness.
A vertical hole bored through the centre (seen from above), as a fraction of the shape width.
How deep the hole goes, measured from the top as a fraction of height. 1 = straight through; smaller leaves a bottom (cup, bowl, planter). Works on solid shapes (blob, thick flesh).
Lattice levels: subdivides faces into a mesh of lines. 0 = none. Adds many skeleton points (useful together with struts).
Density of each lattice level.
Fraction of skeleton points that grow spikes. Shapes with few points (blob, line) get few spikes; add lattice to get many.
Spike length.
Ball on the tip of each spike; 0 = none.
Randomly removes this fraction of lines (thinning). Disconnected pieces are dropped automatically.
Symmetry around the vertical axis: 0 none, 1 mirror, n = n-fold (kaleidoscope-like, also mirrored). Noise obeys it.
Bends the skeleton lines (wobble amplitude).
Wobble frequency: small = slow large waves, large = fine waves.
Lumpiness of the flesh along lines. Has little effect on blob balls.
Lump frequency: small = big lumps, large = fine roughness.
Random seed for every random choice (wobble, lumps, thinning, random membranes). Same seed = same result.
Surface finish (rendering only): 0 glossy, 1 semi-gloss, 2 standard, 3 matte, 4 grainy.
Transparency (rendering only): 0 opaque, 1 slightly translucent, 2 translucent, 3 clear (refractive).
Palette colour index (rendering only).
